findings.description: The option loop uses `shift 2` for --root/--model/--catalog without guarding against a missing value. When one of these flags is the final argument (e.g. `loa-context-class.sh --model $MODEL` with MODEL unset and unquoted), bash's `shift 2` fails with $# == 1 and does not consume anything; because the script runs without `set -e`, the `while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]` loop spins forever on the same `$1`. No shipped call site (hook-guard wiring, loa-status `--show`, the bats tests) passes a dangling flag, so this is not triggered in production today, but it contradicts the header's 'never blocks' contract for any future caller or operator who does.
findings.failure_mode: Infinite loop (100% CPU, never exits) in a script whose contract is to never block; if ever wired that way at SessionStart it would hang session startup.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the value-taking cases fail-safe, e.g. `--root) ROOT="${2:-}"; shift 2 2>/dev/null || break ;;` (same for --model/--catalog), or check `[[ $# -ge 2 ]]` before `shift 2` and otherwise `shift; break`.

findings.cross_file_justification: display_context_line (in diff) and the skills' context-discipline include both read .run/context-class as 'the class this session runs under', but the hook (in diff) writes a single repo-scoped file with last-writer-wins semantics and no session identity.
findings.description: The class is defined as per-session ('the context class this session runs under') but is persisted to a single repo-level file, .run/context-class. Two concurrent Claude Code sessions in the same checkout (common: two terminals, or one with LOA_CONTEXT_CLASS=standard and one without, or different models once the harness exposes `.model`) each fire the once-per-session hook and overwrite each other. `--show` then prints, and the skills then apply, whichever session wrote last. The same staleness arises when the hook does not run for a session (hook-guard skips, hooks disabled, settings not trusted) while a record from an earlier session persists: `--show` trusts the recorded class verbatim with no freshness or session check. The report's atomic mktemp+mv prevents torn writes but not this cross-session clobbering.
findings.failure_mode: A 200K-window session reads `long` (150K full-file threshold) because a sibling 1M session wrote the record after it, or vice versa; /loa reports a class that does not match the running session. Degraded context discipline, not data corruption.
findings.suggested_fix: Record the session id (from the payload `.session_id`) in the second line and have `--show` / readers prefer a per-session path (e.g. .run/context-class.<session_id> with .run/context-class as a fallback), or at minimum document in the include and the /loa line that the record is repo-scoped and may reflect another concurrent session.

findings.description: Payload reading depends on GNU `timeout` (`payload="$(timeout 2 cat 2>/dev/null || true)"`). On macOS without coreutils `timeout` does not exist; the error is swallowed, `payload` is empty, and the `.model` path is silently dead, so the class is always `long` unless LOA_CONTEXT_CLASS is set. The test suite's `stat -f %m` fallback (CC-7) shows macOS is an intended platform, yet no test covers the missing-`timeout` case, and the failure is invisible (exit 0, basis `default`). Impact is nil today if the harness does not yet send `.model`, but it will become a silent misclassification for 200K-model sessions on macOS once it does.
findings.failure_mode: On macOS without GNU coreutils a session on a ≤200K model is classified `long` (20K/50K/30K/150K thresholds) with no error surfaced; the /loa line reports basis `default` giving no hint that model detection was skipped.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard on availability: `if command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then payload="$(timeout 2 cat 2>/dev/null || true)"; else payload="$(cat 2>/dev/null || true)"; fi` (SessionStart stdin is closed by the harness so plain `cat` is safe there), or use bash's `read -t 2` loop. Add a bats case that runs the hook with `timeout` masked off PATH and asserts the payload model is still honoured.

findings.description: The new stub states "this stub keeps the old path and its anchors stable", but it retains only the H1 heading. Every H2 anchor from the original file is gone: #skill-loading-priority, #license-validation-flow, #exit-codes, #environment-variables, #version-control-automatic-gitignore, #security-considerations, #troubleshooting, and the rest. The implementation report says anchor preservation was done only for recommended-hooks §4 and the session-continuity notes-guard recipes, so for this file the stub's own text overstates what it preserves.
findings.failure_mode: Any inbound link of the form constructs-integration.md#exit-codes (or any other H2 fragment) now resolves to the stub with no matching heading, so the fragment silently lands at the top of a four-line file. A reader or agent following such a link gets no content and no indication the section moved. The stub's wording also misleads future maintainers into believing fragment links are safe.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) amend the stub text to say only the path is stable and anchors have moved, or (b) keep the original H2 headings in the stub as one-line pointers to the reference file so fragments still resolve. In both cases grep the repo for 'constructs-integration.md#' and repoint any fragment links to .claude/protocols/reference/constructs-integration.md#<anchor>.

findings.description: The diff replaces `.claude/protocols/citations.md` with a helper-scripts stub pointing to `.claude/protocols/reference/helper-scripts.md`. This removes the active citation protocol from the canonical citations path and redirects consumers to unrelated helper-script documentation.
findings.failure_mode: Any workflow, test, or agent instruction that loads `.claude/protocols/citations.md` will no longer receive the word-for-word citation requirements. That silently disables the grounding/citation contract and causes downstream review/audit outputs to violate the documented citation spec.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not replace `.claude/protocols/citations.md` with the helper-scripts stub. Restore the citation protocol at that path, or if it is being moved, create `.claude/protocols/reference/citations.md` and make the stub point to that citation reference, not `helper-scripts.md`.

findings.cross_file_justification: The sprint AC 'Replay A/B: no gold case loses recall' is evaluated on commit 41b783a1, which includes this protocol relocation. Moving trajectory-evaluation, session-continuity, helper-scripts, recommended-hooks and constructs-integration out of the always-loaded protocol set is a variable in the after arm that the ablation (c9b7bdc0) did not isolate; only the context_discipline include was ablated.
findings.description: The pre-registered gate (per losing case, pooled n=9 after recall >= pooled before recall) failed on all five losing cases: review-pr-02 .926->.815, review-pr-05 .963->.852, audit-pr-02 .852->.815, audit-pr-03 1->.963, audit-pr-05 .926->.889. Missed-defect slots doubled, 5/144 -> 10/144. The pre-registered remedy ('revert or retune the implicated change') was not applied. Instead a post-hoc blind adjudication re-scored 38 of 44 misses as grader defects and the AC is reported as 'met on blind adjudication'. Pre-registration exists precisely to prevent substituting a new measure after seeing the result. The adjudicator's own explanation of the misses (a '(' swallowed into the cited path, continuation citations ':776,807' and 'head:468' that the grader does not parse) describes a change in the after arm's citation output format. That is a behavioural regression in grounding-format compliance, plausibly caused by relocating grounding-adjacent protocols out of the prompt, and it was never ablated. The only ablation tested the include, not the protocol move.
findings.failure_mode: Sprint marked COMPLETED while the production grader (the measure of record until bd-ewrc lands) reports lower recall on five gold cases and the after arm emits citation formats the grader cannot parse. A later re-baseline on bd-ewrc would bake the lower number in and hide whether the protocol move changed model output.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat the AC as unmet, as the report itself states. Either (a) apply the pre-registered remedy: build a second ablation that restores the five protocols to .claude/protocols/ while keeping the context-class work, re-run the five losing cases at n=6, and only then decide whether the move is implicated; or (b) record an explicit human ruling in the review record accepting the deviation, and make bd-ewrc (grader fix plus re-baseline) a blocker for COMPLETED rather than a follow-up. Do not accept 'met on blind adjudication' as satisfying a pre-registered gate.

findings.description: The hunk labelled a/.claude/protocols/citations.md has the context line '# Helper Scripts Reference', removes 517 lines, and installs the helper-scripts stub ('The full text lives at .claude/protocols/reference/helper-scripts.md ... Quick index: .claude/loa/reference/scripts-reference.md'). That is the helper-scripts.md -> stub conversion wearing the wrong path. The supplied full-file context for citations.md shows the Word-for-Word Citation Protocol intact with its Related Protocols line repointed to reference/trajectory-evaluation.md, so this is most likely a diff-generation artefact. If it is real, the citation protocol that reviewing-code and grounding-enforcement.md depend on has been overwritten with an unrelated stub.
findings.failure_mode: If real: loss of the citation protocol, breaking the grounding/citation enforcement chain. If an artefact: the review record attributes the helper-scripts change to citations.md and the actual helper-scripts.md stub diff is absent from the record.
findings.suggested_fix: Run `git diff f4531477 41b783a1 --stat -- .claude/protocols/citations.md .claude/protocols/helper-scripts.md` and confirm citations.md changed only in its Related Protocols line while helper-scripts.md is the 523->6 line stub conversion. Fix the diff rendering if the label is wrong.

findings.description: Every stub asserts 'this stub keeps the old path and its anchors stable', but only the anchors that existing tests grep survive. recommended-hooks.md keeps only '### 4. Memory Injection Hook'; the Setup Hook, once/async, Context Cleanup Hook, Hook Development Guidelines, Disabling Hooks and Provenance anchors are gone from the old path. constructs-integration.md keeps none. The protocol-refs-resolve test checks file paths, not '#fragment' anchors, so a link such as recommended-hooks.md#async-hooks-v210 now resolves to a stub without that section and no test notices. Separately, section 4 now exists verbatim in both the stub and reference/recommended-hooks.md, and the reference copy still carries the Provenance paragraph about section 4. The wording of section 4 is pinned by dead-recall-relabel, so there are now two files that must be edited in lockstep.
findings.failure_mode: Silently broken deep links into the five moved protocols; section 4 wording drifts between stub and reference copy, and a future edit to one file flips dead-recall-relabel or no-history-in-rule-text depending on which path the test reads.
findings.suggested_fix: Grep for fragment links into the moved files, e.g. `grep -rn -E '(recommended-hooks|helper-scripts|trajectory-evaluation|session-continuity|constructs-integration)\.md#' .claude grimoires tests`, and repoint them to reference/ or keep the headings as one-line pointers in the stub. Reduce the stub's section 4 to a one-line pointer at the reference copy (or drop section 4 from the reference copy) so the pinned text lives in exactly one place. Reword the stub sentence to say which anchors are kept.

findings.cross_file_justification: reference/ is the first nested directory under .claude/protocols/. Any script that enumerates protocols with a non-recursive glob now silently excludes these five files.
findings.description: The report concedes that migrate-skill-names.sh and loa-eject.sh loop over .claude/protocols/*.md without reference/. The same pattern is likely in check-loa.sh (System Zone sha256 integrity), update.sh step 6 Restore Overrides and step 8 Generate Checksums, and the enumerator behind tools/check-prompt-budget.sh. The budget drop (199,593 -> 131,078 B) matches the budget tool excluding reference/, which is intended. The same exclusion in the integrity path is not: if the checksum manifest is built from a non-recursive glob, the five moved protocols fall outside System Zone integrity checking, and reference/helper-scripts.md documents the exact curl-pipe-bash install and update command lines users are told to run.
findings.failure_mode: Tampering with any reference/ protocol goes undetected by check-loa.sh; update.sh's restore-overrides or atomic swap treats nested files differently from top-level ones; eject leaves an orphan reference/ tree.
findings.suggested_fix: Run `grep -rn 'protocols/\*\.md' .claude/scripts tools .claude/hooks` and decide recursive vs. non-recursive explicitly for each hit. Ensure the checksum manifest includes reference/*.md and add a test asserting every file under .claude/protocols/**/*.md appears in the manifest.

findings.description: The diff for .claude/protocols/session-continuity.md (index e57ff4ae..08c01032) is cut off after the +++ header, so the stub content is not reviewable. The report says this stub retains the notes-guard recipes that the notes-template tests grep. In the reference copy, exactly one hard-coded threshold ('Yellow threshold (5,000 tokens)') was replaced with the context-class pointer; 5,000 is the standard-class accumulated value and contradicts the long default of 50K. Any recipe text retained in the stub, or any other threshold mention in the reference copy outside the single changed hunk, that still reads 5,000 would tell a long-class session to run Delta-Synthesis at a tenth of its budget.
findings.failure_mode: Stub and reference copy disagree with tool-result-clearing.md on when Delta-Synthesis fires; agents reading the stub apply standard-class thresholds in long-class sessions.
findings.suggested_fix: Run `grep -n -E '5,?000|8,?000|Yellow|Red threshold' .claude/protocols/session-continuity.md .claude/protocols/reference/session-continuity.md` and replace remaining fixed numbers with the class-table pointer. Include the full stub diff in the review record.

findings.description: The diff replaces `.claude/protocols/citations.md` with a Session Continuity stub pointing to `reference/session-continuity.md`. That leaves the citation protocol path no longer containing citation rules, while other protocol text still treats `citations.md` as the citation-format source.
findings.failure_mode: Agents or validators that load `.claude/protocols/citations.md` for citation requirements will read session-continuity guidance instead, so citation enforcement can silently stop applying or apply the wrong protocol.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the word-for-word citation protocol at `.claude/protocols/citations.md`, or if the intent was to stub a moved citation protocol, point it to the correct citation reference file and keep the title/content aligned with citations rather than session continuity.

findings.description: The sprint acceptance criterion 'Replay A/B: no gold case loses recall' is unmet on its own pre-registered terms. The gate fixed before extra trials (pooled n=9 after >= before, per losing case) fails on all five losing cases (review-pr-02, review-pr-05, audit-pr-02, audit-pr-03, audit-pr-05). Missed-defect slots doubled from 5/144 to 10/144. The pre-registered remedy ('revert or retune the implicated change') was not applied; instead a post-hoc blind adjudication re-scored the misses, and even on that measure audit-pr-02 still loses (0.963 vs 1.000). The adjudication itself attributes the grader drops to citation-format changes in the after arm (paren swallowed into path, continuation citations `:776,807`, `head:468`), which means the instruction diet did change output format, not just grader luck. The ablation only clears the context_discipline include; the protocol stubs (this hunk and session-continuity), the CLAUDE.loa.md trim, and the constraints rationale rewrite remain un-bisected.
findings.failure_mode: Measured recall regression in the reviewing-code and auditing-security skills ships to every consumer of the framework; downstream parsers that rely on the citation format (grader, verdict-trailer tooling) see more unparseable citations. The gate was moved after the result was known.
findings.suggested_fix: Hold the merge until one of: (a) bisect the remaining suspects (protocol stubs vs CLAUDE.loa.md trim vs constraints rationales) with the same 6-trial protocol and revert the implicated move per the pre-registered remedy; or (b) obtain explicit human sign-off to amend the AC, land the grader fix (bd-ewrc) test-first, re-baseline, and re-run the five losing cases before COMPLETED. Do not let the post-hoc adjudicated measure replace the pre-registered one without that sign-off.

findings.description: The new protocol text fails open: 'when it is absent, assume `long`', and the report states every hook error path (yq missing, catalog miss, alias unresolved, sanitiser rejecting the model id) also resolves to `long`. `long` thresholds are 10x the `standard` ones (150,000-token session total). On a <=200K model such as claude-haiku-4-5-20251001, 150K of accumulated tool results plus system prompt and skills exceeds Claude Code's auto-compact trigger, so compaction fires before the protocol's STOP-and-synthesize point. That is exactly the information loss the 'Clear, Don't Compact' paradigm exists to prevent.
findings.failure_mode: Haiku 4.5 (or any <=200K catalog model) on a machine without yq, or any session where SessionStart hooks did not run (hooks disabled, hook-guard skip, missing .run/), silently operates under long-class thresholds and loses un-synthesized decisions to auto-compaction.
findings.suggested_fix: Invert the fail-safe direction: unknown or error -> `standard`; only an affirmative catalog lookup with context_window > 200000 (or LOA_CONTEXT_CLASS=long) selects `long`. If the default must stay `long` for the Claude 5 majority, at minimum emit a visible warning line in `/loa` and the hook stderr when the class was chosen by fallback rather than lookup, and add a CC test for the yq-absent path on a 200K model.

findings.cross_file_justification: The protocol text in this hunk instructs agents to trust `.run/context-class`; that file is written by `.claude/hooks/session-start/loa-context-class.sh`, which the report says is registered behind hook-guard.sh with `once` and only on SessionStart.
findings.description: `.run/context-class` is computed once per session at SessionStart. Claude Code allows switching models mid-session via `/model`, and `LOA_CONTEXT_CLASS` can change between prompts; neither re-fires SessionStart. The record therefore goes stale: a session that starts on a 1M model and switches to a 200K model keeps `long` thresholds for the rest of the session. Two concurrent sessions in the same checkout with different models also race on the single file, last writer wins.
findings.failure_mode: Agent reads a stale `long` record on a 200K model after a mid-session model switch and over-accumulates tool results (see DISS-002 failure mode).
findings.suggested_fix: Record the model id alongside the class in `.run/context-class` (or a sibling file) and have the context_discipline include tell the agent to re-derive when the current model differs; or re-run the hook from a UserPromptSubmit hook with a cheap model-id compare. Document the staleness window in tool-result-clearing.md if not fixed.

findings.cross_file_justification: The removed text states that `pre-compact-marker.sh` and `post-compact-reminder.sh` 'inject the recovery sequence' and point at this protocol; `/run sprint-plan` unattended recovery and `br sync --flush-only` at session end were specified only here.
findings.description: The stub drops operational instructions that are not reference material: (1) Phase 1 step 0 'Run mode first: if `.run/sprint-plan-state.json` has state RUNNING, resume sprints.current immediately, no interactive recovery, no confirmation', which the removed text says 'is what lets /run sprint-plan survive context compaction during unattended execution'; (2) 'Always run `br sync --flush-only` at session end'; (3) Fork Detection / ledger-wins rule. These are now outside the prompt budget behind a pointer. The report claims 'No enforcement text was removed' but these are behavioral directives, not rationales. Unless post-compact-reminder.sh, CLAUDE.loa.md, or the run-state-surface hook output carry the run-mode resume instruction verbatim, an agent recovering from compaction mid-run sees only the notes-guard table and may stop to ask for confirmation.
findings.failure_mode: Unattended `/run sprint-plan` stalls on a confirmation prompt after compaction, or ends a session without flushing beads, losing task state.
findings.suggested_fix: Either keep the run-mode step 0 and the `br sync --flush-only` line in the stub (they are under 300 bytes), or verify and cite in the report that post-compact-reminder.sh / CLAUDE.loa.md emit them independently, with a test that greps the hook output for `sprint-plan-state.json` and `RUNNING`.

findings.cross_file_justification: The thresholds became class-dependent in this hunk, but the texts moved verbatim to `.claude/protocols/reference/trajectory-evaluation.md` and `.claude/protocols/reference/session-continuity.md` (and, per synthesis-checkpoint.md's link, `attention-budget.md`) still hardcode the old single-class numbers.
findings.description: The moved reference text still says 'apply Tool Result Clearing if result_count > 20 or tokens_estimated > 2000', 'delta_sync phase is logged at the 5,000-token accumulated threshold (see tool-result-clearing.md)', and 'Run Delta-Synthesis at the Yellow threshold (5,000 tokens)'. Under the `long` class the live protocol says 20,000 / 50,000. An agent that follows the stub's pointer gets contradictory numbers, and the delta_sync trajectory field `tokens: 5000` no longer describes when the sync actually fires.
findings.failure_mode: Agents and the reviewing-code trajectory audit disagree on when clearing and delta-sync were required; audit flags compliant long-class sessions as late, or agents on `long` clear at 2K anyway, negating the diet.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the hardcoded numbers in the moved reference files and attention-budget.md with 'the class threshold in tool-result-clearing.md' or with both class values; add the two reference files to the protocol-refs-resolve or a threshold-consistency test.

findings.description: The first hunk is labeled `a/.claude/protocols/citations.md` but its removed content is the Session Continuity Protocol and its replacement is the session-continuity stub, while the supplied full-file context for citations.md shows the intact Word-for-Word Citation Protocol (with only the trajectory-evaluation pointer repointed). One of the two inputs is wrong. If the diff path is accurate, the citations protocol (grounding ratio rule, negative grounding, self-audit) was overwritten with a stub; if the full file is accurate, the diff was mislabeled by the review harness and the real citations.md change is a one-line repoint.
findings.failure_mode: If the diff path is literal, the citation protocol that synthesis-checkpoint Step 1 and the grounding-check script depend on is gone from the live tree.
findings.suggested_fix: Run `git show --stat 41b783a1 -- .claude/protocols/citations.md .claude/protocols/session-continuity.md` and confirm citations.md changed by one line and session-continuity.md is the 438->10 line stub. Fix the review-harness path mapping if that is the cause.

findings.description: The stub says it 'keeps the old path and its anchors stable' but changes the Level 2 recovery recipe: the removed text (and therefore the moved reference file) defines Level 2 as `ck --hybrid "..." grimoires/loa/ --top-k 3 --jsonl` (~200-500 tokens), while the stub defines Level 2 as `notes-guard.sh read --file F --section <H>` with `--index`. The in-budget stub and the out-of-budget reference now disagree on what Level 2 is, and the stub relies on `--file`, `--section`, and `--index` flags whose existence in notes-guard.sh is not evidenced in the report.
findings.failure_mode: An agent following the stub runs a notes-guard.sh invocation that may be rejected if those flags do not exist; an agent following the reference runs ck instead; recovery behavior differs by which file was read.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm `notes-guard.sh read --file --section --index` exist (and are covered by notes-template.bats); update the Level 2 row in reference/session-continuity.md to match the stub, or restore the ck recipe in the stub.

findings.description: The generated Agent Teams constraint block in `CLAUDE.loa.md` was not regenerated after the corresponding rationales changed in `.claude/data/constraints.json`. The file still contains the old shorter rationale text and the old generated hash (`c020-teamcreate`) for `agent_teams_constraints`.
findings.failure_mode: Generated instruction artifacts drift from their source of truth. Any validation that checks generated constraint blocks against `.claude/data/constraints.json` will fail, and agents consuming `CLAUDE.loa.md` receive stale rationale text despite the source update.
findings.suggested_fix: Regenerate `CLAUDE.loa.md` from `.claude/data/constraints.json` so the `agent_teams_constraints` block text and hash match the updated source, or revert the source rationale edits if they were not intended to affect generated instructions.

findings.description: Sprint AC 'Replay A/B: no gold case loses recall' is not met by the change under review. The pre-registered gate (pooled n=9, after >= before per case, fixed before extra trials ran) failed on five cases: review-pr-02 .926->.815, review-pr-05 .963->.852, audit-pr-02 .852->.815, audit-pr-03 1->.963, audit-pr-05 .926->.889. Missed-defect slots doubled from 5/144 to 10/144, concentrated on D13-find-exec-multi-root (0/6 -> 3/6) and D06-prerelease-tags-rejected (1/6 -> 3/6). The pre-registered remedy (revert or retune the implicated change) was not applied; a post-hoc LLM adjudication was substituted as the measure, and even on that measure audit-pr-02 still loses (.963 vs 1.000). The ablation commit c9b7bdc0 restored only this include and left the long-class thresholds table in tool-result-clearing.md, the five protocol moves, and the CLAUDE.loa.md diet in place, so 'the include is not what moves the grader' does not exclude the other diff-touched changes (kernel truenames/Reference collapse, constraint rationale cuts) as the cause; the before arm (main 2079e719) has none of them.
findings.failure_mode: reviewing-code and auditing-security ship with a measured recall regression on the gold set. Defects of the D13 (multi-root find -exec) and D06 (prerelease tag rejection) classes pass the review and audit gates in roughly half of trials instead of 0-1 in 6. The gates are the framework's only check that code meets acceptance and security criteria (per C-PROC rationale in this same diff), so the regression is a production quality exposure, not a test artefact.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat the pre-registered gate as binding. Either (a) revert the default to standard thresholds (or the full Sprint 3 diet) until bd-ewrc lands and a re-baselined A/B passes the registered gate on the fixed grader, or (b) run a proper component ablation: after-tree minus include, after-tree minus protocol thresholds table, after-tree minus kernel diet, each at n=9 on the five losing cases, and revert the component that moves recall. Do not accept a post-hoc adjudicated measure as the AC gate; record the decision in the audit, not the implementer report.

findings.cross_file_justification: The diff edits the why field of the five C-TEAM constraints (constraints.json hunks at 1232, 1253, 1274, 1295, 1316). The rendered agent_teams_constraints block in CLAUDE.loa.md, which claims to be generated from constraints.json, was not touched by the regeneration and its Why text matches neither the old nor the new why.
findings.description: Five of the twelve tightened rationales have no rendered effect. generate-constraints.sh was re-run and the process_compliance_never/always hashes changed (74e01d57->2fe3c087, bcb45bf9->811c6b84), but the agent_teams_constraints block kept the static non-hash marker 'hash:c020-teamcreate' and Why text such as 'Planning skills assume single-writer semantics' and 'SQLite single-writer prevents lock contention', which match neither the pre- nor post-diff why. Either the block is hand-maintained under a 'DO NOT EDIT - generated from constraints.json' marker, or the generator renders it from a different field. prompt-audit-generated-blocks passed 3/3 with this divergence, so the drift check does not cover the block. The report's 'twelve rationales tightened ... golden tables re-rendered' holds for seven.
findings.failure_mode: Future edits to C-TEAM why strings silently never reach the kernel prompt, and the generated/DO-NOT-EDIT marker gives a false guarantee. Anyone correcting an Agent Teams rationale in constraints.json (e.g. after an incident) will believe the kernel updated when it did not.
findings.suggested_fix: Either make generate-constraints.sh render agent_teams_constraints from why (or a declared short-why field) with a real content hash and add the block to the prompt-audit-generated-blocks drift check, or remove the generated marker from that section and revert the five no-op constraints.json edits so the source of truth is not misleading.

findings.description: The include fixes long as the default class, and per the report the SessionStart hook resolves every error path to long. The permissive class is therefore the fail-open outcome for a <=200K model whenever detection fails: payload lacks .model, catalog alias miss, yq absent, or the hook not wired in a consumer repo that only merged one of the two settings files. Long thresholds are 20K single / 50K accumulated / 30K full file / 150K session, i.e. 75% of a 200K window before the extraction rule fires, on top of kernel, skills, and includes.
findings.failure_mode: On a 200K-window session (e.g. Haiku 4.5) with detection failure, the agent follows long-class discipline, never extracts to NOTES.md, exhausts context, and compacts mid-task. The compaction destroys exactly the cross-session state the discipline exists to preserve, and Run Mode Recovery then resumes from a NOTES.md that was never updated.
findings.suggested_fix: Fail closed: resolve unknown model and error paths to standard, select long only on a positive catalog match >200K or an explicit LOA_CONTEXT_CLASS=long, and change the include wording to 'standard when the class is unknown'. Add a CC test for the no-.model / no-catalog path asserting standard.

findings.description: Two pieces of operative guidance were dropped from the include without a skill-reachable replacement. (a) The NOTES.md routing clause 'decisions -> Decision Log, issues -> Technical Debt' is gone; with session-continuity.md moved to .claude/protocols/reference/ behind a stub in this same sprint, the routing rule is now two hops from any skill. (b) The protocol reference shrank from .claude/protocols/tool-result-clearing.md to the bare tool-result-clearing.md. This sprint created a second protocols directory (protocols/reference/), so a bare name is now ambiguous, and bare names are invisible to protocol-refs-resolve, so a future move of that file would not be caught.
findings.failure_mode: Agents append decisions and debt into Session Continuity or arbitrary sections; notes-guard section reads and Decision Log consumers miss them, and the 'reason from the synthesis' step degrades. A skill loaded without the protocols tree in context may fail to locate the thresholds file by bare name.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full protocol path (19 bytes) and a short routing clause such as 'decisions -> Decision Log, debt -> Technical Debt' (about 45 bytes, within the include's headroom), or move the routing rule into the NOTES.md template header where notes-guard surfaces it on every read.

findings.description: The sprint's own acceptance criterion for this change (sprint.md Sprint 3: 'Replay A/B: no gold case loses recall') failed on the pre-registered metric. Pooled n=9 graded recall dropped on five of the gold cases (review-pr-02 .926→.815, review-pr-05 .963→.852, audit-pr-02 .852→.815, audit-pr-03 1→.963, audit-pr-05 .926→.889) and missed-defect slots doubled (5/144 → 10/144), concentrated on D13 and D06. The pre-registered remedy ('revert or retune the implicated change') was not applied. Instead the gate was re-adjudicated after the fact by an Opus 5.5 model judge, which is the same model family as the implementing subagent, and 38 of 44 misses were reclassified as grader defects. Pre-registration exists precisely so a failed gate cannot be rescued by post-hoc reinterpretation; the grader defects claimed (a '(' swallowed into a path, ignored continuation citations, a single-anchor D13) are mechanical and should be demonstrated deterministically, not by model judgement. The changelog entry added in this hunk records the context-discipline change as shipped without noting the failed gate.
findings.failure_mode: The context-discipline change (long-class thresholds as default, parallelism gates removed, five protocols moved out of the loaded set) merges with a measured recall regression on the gold corpus that the sprint's own gate was designed to catch. If the adjudication is wrong, reviewers and auditors downstream miss more defects (D13-class multi-root find/exec and D06-class prerelease-tag bugs) on every subsequent sprint, with no further gate to catch it.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not merge on the post-hoc adjudication alone. Either (a) fix the grader test-first under bd-ewrc (unit tests pinning the three parsing failures named in the report), re-baseline both arms with the fixed grader, and re-run the pre-registered gate on all five losing cases; or (b) apply the pre-registered remedy for the implicated move and re-run. Record whichever path is taken, and the gate outcome, in the changelog entry and the sprint report rather than only in replay-ab.md.

findings.description: The re-chosen thresholds are calibrated against the current tree with no operating margin in either direction. PROTO_WARN is 114,688 B while the protocols total after the diet is 131,078 B, so the human-mode run prints 'WARN: protocols total ... exceeds the 114688 B warning threshold' on every CI run from day one, which is the same persistent-warning state the old 143,360 threshold produced against 199,593 B. LOA_LIMIT is 9,216 B against a CLAUDE.loa.md of 9,199 B, leaving 17 bytes; any single-word rationale edit or an added table row breaks CI.
findings.failure_mode: A warning that fires unconditionally is ignored, so the warn tier stops functioning as an early signal. A 17-byte ceiling turns every ordinary edit to CLAUDE.loa.md into a budget breach, which pushes contributors to trim unrelated text or move content into uncounted files to land changes.
findings.suggested_fix: Either set PROTO_WARN above the post-diet total (e.g. 140,000 B) so the warn tier means 'growth since the diet', or trim protocols below 114,688 B before landing. Give CLAUDE.loa.md a documented margin (a few hundred bytes) or trim the file further so the limit is a ceiling rather than the current size plus 17.

findings.description: The header now states '(reference/ is not counted)' and the tool's own charging rule says 'the byte budget cannot be met by moving text into a file the skill still always loads'. The exclusion is implemented only by the non-recursive glob '.claude/protocols/*.md', and the charging regex RES matches only 'resources/<name>.md'. A SKILL.md, a counted protocol, or CLAUDE.loa.md that says 'Read `.claude/protocols/reference/helper-scripts.md`' with no guard word is not charged anywhere. Roughly 68 KB of protocol text left the counted set in this sprint behind stubs that point at the new location; nothing in the tool or the test suite asserts the moved files are reached only via guarded pointers, so the diet is enforced by convention.
findings.failure_mode: The always-loaded surface can grow without bound through protocols/reference/ while check-prompt-budget.sh reports green, defeating the gate this change tightens. A future unguarded 'Read reference/X' in a skill silently reintroduces the context pressure the sprint set out to remove.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the charging rule so an unguarded read imperative naming '.claude/protocols/reference/<name>.md' in a SKILL.md or in a counted protocol charges that file's bytes to the referrer, and add a bats case that an unguarded reference/ read breaches. Alternatively add a lint test asserting every occurrence of 'protocols/reference/' in SKILL.md, protocols/*.md and CLAUDE.loa.md is on a line containing a GUARD word.

findings.cross_file_justification: The hook .claude/hooks/session-start/loa-context-class.sh is not in the diff, but this diff-touched hunk states its contract: 'it never blocks and every error path is `long`'. The report confirms the hook depends on yq, the model catalog and the session payload's model field.
findings.description: The context class fails open. 'long' selects thresholds ten times larger than 'standard' (20K/50K/30K/150K vs 2K/5K/3K/15K). Every error path (yq absent, catalog unreadable, payload missing .model, alias unresolved, unknown model id) resolves to 'long' rather than to the conservative class. A session on a 200K-window model whose hook hits any of those paths is told it may keep 30K full-file reads and a 150K session, which is the wrong direction to fail on exactly the class of model the discipline exists to protect.
findings.failure_mode: On a host without yq or with a stale catalog, a 200K-window session adopts long-class thresholds, fills its context, and degrades mid-sprint with no record that the class was a fallback rather than a resolution.
findings.suggested_fix: When the model cannot be resolved to a catalog entry (as opposed to resolving to one with context_window > 200000), fall back to 'standard', or at minimum write the reason into .run/context-class alongside the class so /loa prints 'long (fallback: yq missing)' and the operator can pin LOA_CONTEXT_CLASS. Add a CC case covering the yq-absent and unknown-model paths.

findings.description: The sprint AC 'Replay A/B: no gold case loses recall' is unmet on the pre-registered measure. Pooled n=9 recall fell on review-pr-02 (.926 to .815), review-pr-05 (.963 to .852), audit-pr-02 (.852 to .815), audit-pr-03 (1 to .963) and audit-pr-05 (.926 to .889); missed-defect slots went 5/144 to 10/144, with D13 misses 0/6 to 3/6 and D06 1/6 to 3/6. The pre-registered remedy (revert or retune the implicated change) was not applied. A post-hoc blind adjudication reclassified 38 of 44 misses as grader artifacts, but even on that adjudicated measure audit-pr-02 still loses recall (1.000 to .963), so the AC fails under both measures. The implicated change is the regenerated context_discipline include in this diff, which raises the default thresholds tenfold (full file 3K to 30K before extraction) across auditing-security, implementing-tasks and reviewing-code.
findings.failure_mode: Merging accepts a measured review and audit recall regression on gold defects (D13 find-exec multi-root, D06 prerelease tags) on the implementer's own override of a pre-registered gate. If the adjudication is wrong, the regression ships silently into every /review-sprint and /audit-sprint run. The gate exists precisely to prevent post-hoc reinterpretation of a failed result.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not accept the AC on the implementer's override. Choose one: (a) land the grader fix (bd-ewrc) test-first, re-baseline both arms on the fixed grader, and re-run the five losing cases to show pooled after >= before; (b) apply the pre-registered remedy by shipping the include with the old 2K/5K/3K/15K thresholds as default until parity is demonstrated; or (c) the reviewer records an explicit AC waiver that names the audit-pr-02 D06 loss as accepted, citing the c9b7bdc0 ablation as the basis.

findings.description: ride.md was touched only to repoint the session-continuity path, but the same file still instructs 'Monitor attention budget (advisory, not blocking)' and 'Trigger Delta-Synthesis at Yellow threshold (5k tokens)'. After this diff the default class is long with an accumulated threshold of 50K; 5k is the standard-class accumulated threshold. The diff-touched context-engineering.md also states attention-budget zones were deleted in cycle-121.
findings.failure_mode: /ride agents receive two contradictory thresholds (5k vs 50K) plus a reference to a mechanism documented as removed. The skill either over-synthesizes on long-class sessions or ignores the command text, and the stale Yellow-zone wording contradicts the protocol the include now cites.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the 5k Yellow line with a pointer to the class thresholds in tool-result-clearing.md (accumulated threshold for the class in .run/context-class) and drop the attention-budget wording from the During Session block.

findings.cross_file_justification: The diff-touched PARALLEL-REVIEW.md and PARALLEL-SPLIT.md headers and the three SKILL.md Phase -1 sections now point at resources/REFERENCE.md ('has the size table') and a parallel_threshold key; neither REFERENCE.md file nor any config/schema file is modified in this diff.
findings.description: The size tables previously lived inline in each SKILL.md Phase -1 and are deleted here. The replacement text says 'Parallelise (parallel_threshold) when the scope warrants' and the two resource headers say 'REFERENCE.md has the size table'. No hunk in this diff adds a size table to auditing-security/resources/REFERENCE.md or reviewing-code/resources/REFERENCE.md, and no hunk defines parallel_threshold in .loa.config.yaml.example or its schema. The implementation report does not list REFERENCE.md among the edited files.
findings.failure_mode: If those targets do not exist, 'large scope' and 'large sprint' have no definition reachable from the skills, the lead's parallel decision becomes guesswork, and the pointer reintroduces by reference the size gate the AC says was removed.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify both REFERENCE.md files contain the size table and that parallel_threshold exists in the config example and schema. If either is absent, add it or change the pointers to 'the lead decides' with no table or key reference.

findings.description: The include tells agents to treat long (20K/50K/30K/150K) as the default whenever .run/context-class is absent, and the hooks-reference row documents that the hook resolves every error path to long. Hooks are opt-in (README: install via /mount or manual merge), so any project without hooks, any session before the hook runs, and any model id missing from the catalog gets the permissive class regardless of window size.
findings.failure_mode: A 200K-window session (Sonnet, Haiku, or any model not in the catalog) follows a 150K session threshold and 30K full-file reads before extracting to NOTES.md, consuming most of the window before the discipline engages. For a limit whose purpose is to protect smaller contexts, defaulting to the permissive class is fail-open.
findings.suggested_fix: Fail closed: treat a missing or unreadable record or an unknown model as standard, and select long only on positive catalog evidence of a >200K window or an explicit LOA_CONTEXT_CLASS=long. Update the include text and both hook table rows to match.

findings.description: .run/context-class is one project-local word derived from the session model, written at SessionStart behind hook-guard once. It is shared by every session in the same checkout and read by every subagent that loads a SKILL.md carrying the include. Two concurrent sessions on different models in one directory (a 1M lead plus a 200K helper terminal) race with last-writer-wins. The parallel_execution Explore and category subagents dispatched by a long lead may run on 200K models yet read long from the shared record.
findings.failure_mode: A 200K session or subagent applies 150K session and 30K full-file thresholds inside a 200K window. The once guard also means a mid-session /model switch to a smaller model never refreshes the record.
findings.suggested_fix: Key the record by session id (for example .run/context-class.<session_id>, or embed the session id and verify on read). Have the three skills' parallel dispatch pass the class explicitly to subagents, or default subagents to standard unless their model is known to be long-window.

findings.description: The Hook Registry table gains the SessionStart row for session-start/loa-context-class.sh, but the same file's 'Active (registered in settings.hooks.json)' table, which manual installers use to know what to merge into ~/.claude/settings.json, is not updated. The registry also still omits the other SessionStart hooks (loa-kf-surface.sh, loa-run-state-surface.sh) that hooks-reference.md lists as registered.
findings.failure_mode: Operators following the Files table omit the hook, .run/context-class is never written, and per DISS-004 the session silently runs the permissive long class.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the loa-context-class.sh row to the Active table and reconcile the registry with hooks-reference.md so the two documents list the same SessionStart hooks.
